articles.snippet: Young people in Britain’s poorer towns have far fewer opportunities. Although 84% of Neets say they want to work, their prospects are unfairly limited by where they live. Rotherham has one suitable vacancy for every 22 young adults. articles.title: Bert Schulpen (94) maakt al 80 jaar muziek, even lang als de academie van Maaseik bestaat
articles.snippet: Bert Schulpen hoorde in 1946 bij de eerste leerlingen van de academie van Maaseik. Tot voor kort speelde hij nog muziek in het woonzorgcentrum waar hij nu woont. Hij verzorgt morgen als oudste ex-leerling het voorwoord van de viering van 80 jaar kunstonderwijs in Maaseik.

articles.title: ‘I spend a bagful of money and don’t fill a bag’: the energy crisis hits Bangladesh
articles.snippet: The country has been left in the dark as it endures power cuts caused by the Iran war and reliance on gas imports At 1am, Halder’s alarm goes off and the 34-year-old Bangladeshi bank employee rises and heads to her kitchen. She is up at this time not for work but to cook for her family. An energy crisis paralysing the capital, Dhaka, a city of almost 40 million people , means this has become the only time when the piped gas supply is strong enough to allow cooking. The city now operates in darkness, as people try to continue their lives with power even in public areas shut off early in the evening to preserve energy. Continue reading...
